summary: Every element appears twice except one; find the one that appears once in O(n) time and O(1) space.
mainInsight: XOR is commutative and associative with x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x, so XOR-ing the whole array cancels every pair and leaves the single element.

approaches.name: Hash map / set
approaches.summary: Count occurrences or toggle membership in a set.

approaches.name: Math (2*sum(set) - sum)
approaches.summary: Twice the sum of distinct values minus the array sum.

personalSolution.notes: Optimal and well explained in your docstring.

cards.explanation: x ^ x = 0 cancels pairs and x ^ 0 = x preserves the survivor.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Bitwise NOT: NOT is unary and does not combine elements.

promptVariants: Why does XOR-ing all numbers leave only the single one, regardless of order?
Why do the pairs cancel under XOR even when they are not adjacent?
cards.answer: XOR is commutative and associative, so duplicates can be brought together: (A^A) ^ (C^C) ^ B = 0 ^ 0 ^ B = B.
cards.explanation: That is exactly the derivation in your docstring.

cards.answer: When duplicates appear three times, not twice (Single Number II)
cards.explanation: XOR cancels pairs only; for triples you must count bits modulo 3 (or use two accumulators).
